Inkling logo directions
01020304050607080910111213

Loose Threads · logo directions · 6 November 2026

Thirteen marks for Inkling, each made from the app's own thread

All thirteen in one Dock

All thirteen in one Dock at 64 pt, today's at the left. Point along it to magnify, as the Dock does; click one to jump to it.

Why today's mark doesn't fit

  • It draws the tools, not the stitches. The icon is an illustration: a wooden hoop, a brass screw, a steel needle, wood and metal gradients. The app itself only ever draws thread on a flat page.
  • Its colour belongs to someone else. The tile is indigo, which in the app is another mind's thread. Inkling's own is madder, on linen or lamplight.
  • It falls apart small. At 32 px and below the hoop reads as a clock face and the stitched question mark disappears.
  • The knot sits on the word like a sticker. In the wordmark it is drawn 1.4 times the width of the dot it replaces (1.7 times in the app's sidebar), in three tones, so it reads as a swirl rather than a dot.

What every direction here keeps

  • Flat colour and the app's own stitch geometry from src/stitch.rs: capsule stitches, a knot with one lighter coil, tapered thread. An object keeps its materials (a reel is still wood) but is drawn flat, without the gradients and bevels of today's icon.
  • Madder for Inkling's thread; linen and lamplight for the ground. Other thread colours appear only where the object has more than one.
  • Letters are Fraunces Display (opsz 72, SOFT 100, WONK 0), outlined from the font the app bundles, so a wordmark matches its title bar exactly. Where the dot is a knot, it is drawn 1.16 times the dot's width.
  • Every icon is one full rounded square, so macOS 26 never puts it in a grey tile, and every one has a dark version.
Today, for comparison: the icon at 96, 32 and 16 pt, and the wordmark

The directions

Each one starts from a different object. Icons show light and dark; the wordmark follows the page's Linen or Lamplight switch. Shortlist the ones worth another round, and leave pointers in a direction's notes: the page keeps them and copies them out for chat.

01

Knot

Inkling lives in the dot of the i, so the whole mark is that dot: one French knot, drawn the way the app draws it.

Risk. Large, the coil reads as a spiral sweet; under 32 px it is a red dot, close to a notification badge.

02

Tied off

The end of every thread in the app: a loose end, tied. The mark is the moment a question is answered.

Risk. Under 32 px it is a squiggle, and a knotted line is also the stock mark for sailing and climbing.

03

Initial

Mark the app the way linen was always marked as someone's own: a satin-stitched i, dotted with a knot.

Risk. A lone i on a tile is the info symbol at 16 and 32 px, and the satin only shows from 128 px up.

04

Sampler

Inkling signs its work the way samplers were signed: ik in counted cross-stitch, with a French knot for the dot.

Risk. Pixel letters can read as an 8-bit game rather than thread, and ik means nothing to a stranger.

05

Needle

Stood on end, a needle is an i: its eye sits where the dot would, and Inkling's thread runs through it.

Risk. Needle and thread is the stock mark of tailors and alteration shops, and in the wordmark the needle reads as a capital I.

06

Spool

A reel of madder thread whose loose end climbs and ties a knot above it: an i made of a reel and a knot.

Risk. It says sewing supplies before it says notebook, and at 16 px it is a red barrel.

07

Tag

Every question in the app hangs on one of these; the icon is that tag, on its thread.

Risk. Before it reads as a question, a tag reads as a price, a sale or a shop.

08

Woven label

The whole tile is the label: ribbed madder with the name woven across it, stitched down at both edges.

Risk. The name is all there is, and it cannot be read below 64 px; a label also says clothing brand.

09

Pamphlet

A notebook held together by one thread tied off in its middle: the app's whole story, in how a notebook is bound.

Risk. An open book is the stock icon for reading apps, and the split wordmark can read as two words.

10

Darn

Inkling finds where your words don't hold and you mend them, visibly: madder warp, your ink as the weft.

Risk. A woven square reads as a grid or a waffle, and mending suggests your writing was broken.

11

Loose end

Three stitches and a loose end curling over: a question mark without its dot, before anyone answers it.

Risk. At 19 px the stitched underline reads as a spell-check line, and the icon's dashes can read as loading.

12

One thread

The name in one thread, never lifted: it starts as a loose end, and the knot on the i comes last, the way you dot an i.

Risk. The only direction with drawn letters, which the language otherwise refuses; script marks look alike, and it is a scribble below 64 px.

13

Hoop

Today's idea redrawn flat, in the app's own stitches, holding one motif from the border Inkling stitches as threads are tied.

Risk. At 16 px a ring with a screw reads as a clock; if the hoop itself is what doesn't fit, this doesn't either.

01

Knot

ObjectA French knot: thread wound twice round the needle and taken back down beside where it came up. It is how embroiderers make a dot.

IdeaInkling lives in the dot of the i, so the whole mark is that dot: one French knot, drawn the way the app draws it.

RiskLarge, the coil reads as a spiral sweet; under 32 px it is a red dot, close to a notification badge.

Every mark here is generated, not hand-placed: design/tools/logo_directions.py draws them from the stitch geometry in src/stitch.rs and the palettes in src/theme.rs, outlines letters with outline.py from assets/fonts/FrauncesDisplay-Medium.ttf, and writes design/logo/<nn-name>/wordmark.svg, mark.svg, icon.svg and icon-dark.svg, then this page. Run it with uv run logo_directions.py from design/tools.

The wordmark and mark files follow the reader's light or dark setting on their own; the icons come as a light and a dark file, at 1024 px on the macOS grid (an 824 px rounded square). The clear and tinted variants macOS 26 asks for come with the build, from whichever direction is picked.
